nodes.summary: Two agents share a prior $\mu$ on a finite set $\Omega$ of states and have information partitions $\mathcal P_1, \mathcal P_2$. If at $\omega$ it is common knowledge that agent 1's posterior of $A$ is $q_1$ and agent 2's is $q_2$ (the cell of the meet of $\mathcal P_1$ and $\mathcal P_2$ that contains $\omega$ lies in the event where the posteriors take these values), and that cell is not null, then $q_1 = q_2$.
nodes.title: Agreeing to disagree

nodes.summary: Agents $i \in I$ share a prior $\mu$ on a finite set $\Omega$ of states and have information partitions $\mathcal P_i$. Let $A$ be an event and $q_i$ agent $i$'s posterior of $A$. If at the state $\omega$ it is common knowledge that $q_i = a_i$ for every $i$, and the cell of the meet containing $\omega$ has positive prior probability, then $a_i = a_j$ for all $i, j$: agents with a common prior cannot agree to…
nodes.title: Agreement theorem

nodes.summary: On a finite set $\Omega$ of states, the information cell $P(\omega)$ of a partition, viewed as a finite set so that sums over it can be written. As a set it is the information cell.
nodes.title: Information cell as a finset

nodes.summary: In a partition model, the information of an agent is a partition $\mathcal P$ of the set $\Omega$ of states of the world, here an equivalence relation $r$ on $\Omega$. At the state $\omega$ the agent is told the cell that contains $\omega$, and cannot distinguish $\omega$ from the other states of that cell.
nodes.title: Information cell

nodes.summary: In a dialogue of posteriors, each agent's partition after round $n + 1$ is finer than after round $n$, since each round replaces a partition by a common refinement of it.
nodes.title: Partitions only get finer during a dialogue

nodes.summary: Given information partitions $\mathcal P_i$ and an event $A$, every agent announces its posterior $q_i$ of $A$. Agent $i$'s new partition is the common refinement of $\mathcal P_i$ and the partition of $\Omega$ into the level sets of the profile $\omega \mapsto (q_j(\omega))_j$.
nodes.title: One round of public announcement of posteriors

nodes.summary: Starting from information partitions $\mathcal P_i^{(0)}$, the partitions after $n$ rounds of public announcement of posteriors of the event $A$: where in each round every agent announces its current posterior of $A$ and refines its partition by the level sets of the announced profile.
nodes.title: Dialogue of posteriors

nodes.summary: Finitely many agents share a prior on a finite set $\Omega$ of states. In each round every agent announces publicly its current posterior of the event $A$, and every agent refines its information partition by the level sets of the announced profile of posteriors. Then the partitions stop changing after finitely many rounds $T$, and at round $T$ all agents' posteriors of $A$ are equal at every state whose meet cell…
nodes.title: We can't disagree forever

nodes.summary: An event $E$ is common knowledge at $\omega$ (it contains the meet cell of $\omega$) if and only if, for every finite sequence of agents $i_1, \dots, i_k$ (repetitions allowed, $k \ge 0$), that is, at $\omega$ agent $i_1$ knows that agent $i_2$ knows that … agent $i_k$ knows $E$.
nodes.title: Common knowledge as iterated knowledge

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a function on $\Omega$ that every agent knows, that is, $f$ is constant on every cell of every agent's partition. Then $f$ is constant on the cells of the meet, and the event $\{\omega' : f(\omega') = f(\omega)\}$ is common knowledge at $\omega$.
nodes.title: Values of commonly known functions are common knowledge

nodes.summary: If an event $E$ is common knowledge at $\omega$, then every agent knows at $\omega$ that $E$ is common knowledge: every state of the agent's cell lies in the meet cell of $\omega$, where $E$ is common knowledge.
nodes.title: Common knowledge is known by everyone

nodes.summary: If an event $E$ is common knowledge at $\omega$, it is common knowledge at every state $\omega'$ in the same cell of the meet as $\omega$: both states have the same meet cell.
nodes.title: Common knowledge is constant on the cells of the meet

nodes.summary: Let agents $i$ have information partitions $\mathcal P_i$ of $\Omega$, and let $\mathcal M$ be their meet, the finest partition that is coarser than every $\mathcal P_i$. An event $E$ is common knowledge at $\omega$ when $E$ contains the cell $M(\omega)$ of the meet that contains $\omega$.
nodes.title: Common knowledge

nodes.summary: For agents with knowledge operators $K_i$ and a finite sequence of agents $i_1, \dots, i_k$, the event "agent $i_1$ knows that agent $i_2$ knows that … agent $i_k$ knows $E$"; the empty sequence gives $E$ itself. Repetitions are allowed.
nodes.title: Iterated knowledge along a chain of agents

nodes.summary: For every partition and every event $E$, the event "the agent knows $E$" is contained in $E$: $K(E) \subseteq E$, because the state $\omega$ lies in its own cell $P(\omega)$.
nodes.title: What is known is true

nodes.summary: An agent with information partition $\mathcal P$ knows the event $E \subseteq \Omega$ at the state $\omega$ when its cell is inside the event, $P(\omega) \subseteq E$. The knowledge operator maps $E$ to the event "the agent knows $E$", What is known is true: $K(E) \subseteq E$.
nodes.title: Knowledge operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mathcal P$ be finer than $\mathcal Q$, and let $Q$ be a cell of $\mathcal Q$. If the posterior of $A$ given $\mathcal P$ equals $a$ at every state of $Q$, then Indeed $Q$ is a disjoint union of cells $P_j$ of $\mathcal P$, on each of which $\mu(A \cap P_j) = a\,\mu(P_j)$; summing over $j$ gives the claim. No cell needs to be nonnull: on a null cell $P_j$ both sides vanish.
nodes.title: The tower step of the agreement theorem

nodes.summary: On a finite set of states, the posterior $\mu(A \cap P(\omega))/\mu(P(\omega))$ of the event $A$ at $\omega$ equals the conditional probability $\mu[A \mid P(\omega)]$ of Mathlib (as a real number). This bridges the definition used here with Mathlib's conditional probability measure $\mu(P)^{-1}\,\mu(P \cap \cdot)$; both are $0$ on a null cell.
nodes.title: Posteriors are conditional probabilities

nodes.summary: Suppose one more round of announcing posteriors of $A$ leaves every agent's partition unchanged. Then each agent's posterior is constant on every agent's cells, so its value is common knowledge; by the agreement theorem, at every state whose meet cell is not null all agents' posteriors of $A$ are equal.
nodes.title: At a fixed point of the dialogue, posteriors agree

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a finite set $\Omega$ of states (the common prior) and $\mathcal P$ an agent's information partition. The agent's posterior probability of the event $A$ at the state $\omega$ is It is the conditional probability of $A$ given the cell $P(\omega)$, and agrees with Mathlib's conditional measure $\mu[\,\cdot \mid P(\omega)]$. If the cell is null, Lean's convention $x / 0 = 0$ makes the…
nodes.title: Posterior probability

nodes.summary: On a finite set $\Omega$ with a partition $\mathcal P$, for every real function $f$, each cell $P$ appears $|P|$ times on the right, once for each of its states, with weight $1/|P|$.
nodes.title: Averaging cell sums

nodes.summary: On a finite set with a partition, if the sum of $f$ over every cell vanishes, then the total sum of $f$ vanishes. This is the step "summing over $j$" in Aumann's proof of the agreement theorem.
nodes.title: Summing over the cells (equality)

nodes.summary: On a finite set with a partition, if the sum of $f$ over every cell is nonpositive, then the total sum of $f$ is nonpositive. This is the step "multiplying by $\mathrm{Prob}\,P$ and summing over all $P$ in $\mathcal P^i$" in Aumann's proof of the Main Theorem of 1987.
nodes.title: Summing over the cells (inequality)
